# Strata Property Act

*Strata Property Act*, SBC 1998, c 43, verbatim from the BC Laws consolidation, one item per section, plus the Schedule of Standard Bylaws. Licence `bc-kings-printer`. Every item here is generated by `tools/import-bclaws.ts`; do not edit the text by hand.

## Layout

```
source.json                       the enactment: citation, urls, consolidation ("current to") date,
                                  retrieved_at, parts[] with divisions and sections, omitted[]
part-01/ … part-17/               one folder per Part; s<section>.md per section
schedule-of-standard-bylaws/      bylaw<section>.md per standard bylaw
```

Part and Division membership is recorded in `source.json` (`parts[].sections`, `parts[].divisions`), not in the items, so a section's text holds nothing that is not in the Act.

## Ids, types and citations

| What | id | type | citation | file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Section 135 | `bc.spa.s135` | `act-section` | `Strata Property Act, SBC 1998, c 43, s 135` | `part-07/s135.md` |
| Section 34.1 | `bc.spa.s34.1` | `act-section` | `Strata Property Act, SBC 1998, c 43, s 34.1` | `part-04/s34.1.md` |
| Standard Bylaw 3 | `bc.spa.sched.bylaw3` | `schedule` | `Strata Property Act, SBC 1998, c 43, Schedule of Standard Bylaws, s 3` | `schedule-of-standard-bylaws/bylaw3.md` |

The id copies the section number exactly as BC Laws prints it, dots included (`s34.1`, `s90.3`). Ids name whole sections only, never a subsection or paragraph: those are addressed by the chunk heading path (`section_ref`, for example `Section 135 — Complaint, right to answer and notice of decision > (1)`).

`title` is the section's heading (its marginal note). `source_url` is the section's anchor on the BC Laws Part page (`…/98043_07#section135`; the Schedule is `…/98043_18#section3`).

### Where the Schedule of Standard Bylaws lives, and why

The standard bylaws are part of the Act (its Schedule), so their verbatim text lives here, in the law layer, as `schedule` items. That keeps one copy of the text, under the law-layer checks (citation, source URL, retrieval date, licence). `building-starter/standard-bylaws/` does not repeat the text: a building-layer `standard-bylaw` item is added there only when it has something of its own to say (for example how a standard bylaw applies when a building's registered bylaws are silent), and it cites the matching `bc.spa.sched.bylaw*` item. Duplicating the text in both layers would put two identical passages in retrieval.

## Body format

- `# Section 135 — Complaint, right to answer and notice of decision`, then `## (1)`, `## (2)` for subsections.
- Paragraphs, subparagraphs, clauses and subclauses are nested list items: `- (a)`, `  - (i)`, `    - (A)`, `      - (I)`. Text that follows a list inside the same provision (for example the words after s. 135 (1) (c)) is its own paragraph, in place.
- Defined terms are bold in quotes (`**"common property"**`); Act names and bracketed descriptions are italic, as on BC Laws.
- Words, numbers and punctuation are exactly as published. Whitespace is normalised: non-breaking spaces and line breaks inside a sentence become one ordinary space.
- Repealed paragraphs and subsections inside a current section are kept exactly as BC Laws shows them (for example `(b) [Repealed 2022-41-6.]`).
- **Formulas.** Sections 99, 195, 227, 247, 273 and 278 contain formulas that BC Laws publishes as images. The item links the image (`![formula](…gif)`) and does not transcribe it; its `notes` flag this. TODO: transcribe these formulas by hand during review and check them against BC Laws.

## Repealed and spent sections

Whole sections that are repealed or spent are **not imported**. BC Laws shows them only as a placeholder (`139-140 [Repealed 2022-41-17.]`), which has nothing to retrieve. Each one is listed in `source.json` `omitted[]` with the placeholder text: sections 139–140, 142–145, 189.2–189.3, 189.5 and 189.6 (repealed), 294–321 (spent consequential amendments), and Standard Bylaw 15 (repealed).

## Dates

- `consolidation_date` in `source.json` is the BC Laws "current to" date; `retrieved_at` is the fetch date.
- `in_force_from` is `null` on every item, with a note: the consolidation does not say when each section's current text came into force. Filling it needs the Tables of Legislative Changes (open question 5 in `research/open-questions.md`). The validator allows a null `in_force_from` on statute items only when `notes` explains why.
- `in_force_to` is `null`: every item is the current text.

## Refreshing

```sh
pnpm --dir kb import:bclaws            # fetch the current consolidation and rewrite the items
pnpm --dir kb import:bclaws --offline  # rebuild from the last fetch in kb/.cache/bclaws/
pnpm --dir kb validate && pnpm --dir kb build
```

The importer fetches the whole Act as XML from the CiviX document endpoint (`…/statreg/98043_00_multi/xml`) and the contents page (`…/statreg/98043_00`) for the "current to" date, sequentially with a pause and an identifying User-Agent. Raw downloads stay in `kb/.cache/` (git-ignored).

On a re-run, an item whose text is unchanged keeps its status, review sign-off, `cites` and `supersedes`. An item whose text changed goes back to `draft` and its `notes` say so; review it, and if the old version matters for past events, keep it as a separate item per `research/open-questions.md` question 5. Sections that disappear from BC Laws are reported, not deleted. Topics come from `tools/lib/bclaws-topics.ts`; change them there. Bump `kb/package.json` after a refresh that changes items.

The importer stops, rather than guessing, on any markup it does not recognise.
